\caption{Percentage of aggregate nodes that are incoherent (children do not sum to the parent, relative gap $>1\%$), averaged over up to eight rolling origins. On 6 of the 8 hierarchies the median foundation model is incoherent on most aggregate nodes; the two exceptions (Labour and Electricity) are the hierarchies whose aggregates are dominated by a common smooth component, which independent forecasts reproduce almost exactly. Incoherence does not track model capacity ($0.8$M--$200$M parameters, a factor of $250$): the low values belong to TinyTimeMixer, the smallest and least accurate model, where a flat forecast is trivially closer to coherent. The classical AutoETS is incoherent at comparable rates, and the two trained global models, which forecast every node jointly rather than per series, are incoherent on $16$--$100\%$ of nodes, so the failure is not specific to per-series forecasting but general to any model whose outputs are not projected onto the coupling set.
